why: Every claim in this repository that a mutation is caught, with the edits that produce it and the command that judges it, so the claim is runnable from inside the tree instead of resting on a script that lived in /tmp. Rounds three and four both recorded that defect and both declined to verify the claims; a count of caught mutations names no script, and a claim that names no script is a claim nobody can run. Each row is applied to a *copy* of the tree by scripts/mutate.mjs - nothing under the repository is opened for writing - and the gate `mutation-claims` checks on every commit that each row still applies (its anchor text occurs exactly once) and that every result claim in docs/context.md and docs/f-evidence.md names a row here. A row may carry `expect: "missed"`: that is a rule the mutation did NOT catch, kept as a recorded limitation with its reproduction instead of a claim. No row carries one today: `mutate:fw-direction-sign-ignored` was this ledger's one recorded miss, and it is a claim now that the probe checks its readout against the direction the views carry - the reproduction and the fix are in docs/f-evidence.md §5.2, and scripts/mutate.mjs prints the verdict rather than this file. What no row can establish is that its mutation moves a computed value rather than the shape of an assertion; that is why each row states the rule it attacks, and why scripts/mutate.mjs prints that rule beside the verdict.
